requirements.requirement: Back up /srv/inventory/data from node2 into a dated archive under /var/backups/inventory on node1.
requirements.summary: An end-to-end backup produced inventory-2026-10-01.tar.gz in the required directory. The archived test payload matched the source SHA-256, the archive validated successfully, and another successful backup was observed after both nodes restarted.

requirements.requirement: Run the inventory backup every night.
requirements.summary: A root cron entry schedules the backup daily at 02:15, crond was active and enabled, and the configured backup command succeeded repeatedly, including after restart.

requirements.requirement: Retain only the last seven days of dated inventory archives.
requirements.summary: The installed retention rule removes matching archives older than six completed days. A bounded test directly showed an eight-day-old archive removed and a six-day-old archive retained; the retained test archive was then cleaned up.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. The provider-wide restart protocol was also complete for both nodes: each had a healthy pre-restart state, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity corroborated by lifecycle snapshots, recovered services and data, and a successful post-restart end-to-end backup.
limitations: The source path did not exist initially and was created by the executor, so backup correctness was demonstrated using a synthetic test file rather than pre-existing inventory data.

The cron entry and active scheduler were observed, but the evidence window did not include an actual 02:15 cron-triggered invocation; repeated direct executions established that the scheduled command itself works.
Generic lifecycle snapshots do not inventory the task-specific scripts and archives, so their persistence is established primarily by the executor's direct post-restart observations.

operational_hygiene.summary: Task-related changes were narrowly scoped, permissions and SSH access were restricted, temporary retention-test archives were removed, package health remained intact, no failed services appeared, and no new listening ports were introduced. The only unnecessary retained residue was the synthetic .backup-transfer-check file created for verification: it had a valid bounded-evidence purpose but was left in the source directory and final archive rather than cleaned up after restart verification. All other observed mutations were necessary implementation, verification, correction, cleanup, or mandatory restart-protocol actions.
